import json, openpyxl
from collections import Counter, defaultdict
T = r"C:/Users/eric_rash/.claude/jobs/94392fa1/tmp/"
D = r"G:/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/02_SPORTS/Football/PP_Recruiting/"

# 1. Tackling removal on the 19: recompute share without Tackling for IDL/EDGE rows
res = json.load(open(T + "validation.json"))
COUNTED = {"IDL": ["Get Off", "Pass Rush", "Run Defense", "Tackling"],
           "EDGE": ["Play Speed", "CoD", "Get Off", "Pass Rush", "Run Defense", "Tackling"]}
for r in res:
    for v in r["rows"]:
        if v["Pos"] in COUNTED and v["Team"] in ("tulsa", "ILST", "western-ky", "marshall", "texas-st", "coastal-caro", "southern-miss"):
            t = v["traits"]; c = [k for k in COUNTED[v["Pos"]] if isinstance(t.get(k), (int, float))]
            el = sum(t[k] >= 75 for k in c); c2 = [k for k in c if k != "Tackling"]; el2 = sum(t[k] >= 75 for k in c2)
            print(r["name"], v["Pos"], "with tackling", el, "/", len(c), "without", el2, "/", len(c2), round(el2 / len(c2), 3))

# 2. Alert volume in 008 (Elig 1+, the pre-portal pool)
wb = openpyxl.load_workbook(D + "008. BAYLOR - TELEMETRY x STAQS UNIFIED GRADING (2025 FCS-G6 BASELINE).xlsx", read_only=True, data_only=True)
rb = wb["REVIEW BOARD"].iter_rows(min_row=4, values_only=True)
h = list(next(rb)); rows = [dict(zip(h, x)) for x in rb if x[0]]
ok = [x for x in rows if x["Sample"] == "OK"]
print("sample OK rows", len(ok))
for thr in (85, 90, 95):
    new = Counter(); newfront = Counter()
    for x in ok:
        pi = x["Player Impact"]
        if isinstance(pi, (int, float)) and pi >= thr and x["REVIEW?"] != "Y":
            new[x["Pos"]] += 1
    print(f"PI>={thr} not already REVIEW, by pos:", dict(new), "total", sum(new.values()))
for thr in (5, 10):
    low = Counter(x["Pos"] for x in ok if x["REVIEW?"] == "Y" and isinstance(x["Player Impact"], (int, float)) and x["Player Impact"] <= thr)
    print(f"REVIEW with PI<={thr}:", dict(low), "total", sum(low.values()))
rev = Counter(x["Pos"] for x in ok if x["REVIEW?"] == "Y")
print("current REVIEW sample OK by pos", dict(rev))

# Validation run 2026-09-16: 2025 FCS / G6 bands versus Baylor grades

Next action 1 from `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-2025-baseline-load.md`. This pass
tests the implemented thresholds. It does not tune them.

## Method

- **Graded players:** 000 `POST-PORTAL RECAP` (read only). Of its 44 players (two tables of 22), 19
  have an FCS or Group of Six previous team: 9 in the left table (B12
  championship-caliber transfers to other schools) and 10 in the right table
  (Baylor-acquired transfers). The Power Four rows wait on validation downloads
  (Next 2). The previous teams match the 2025 season (Colandrea UNLV to
  Nebraska), so the 2025 leaderboard season is the season before each transfer.
- **Scratch build:** `scripts/load_leaderboard.py` on the 22 fcs_g6 CSVs, no
  `--min-elig`, template 003, written through Excel COM to the job temp folder,
  not Drive. 14,068 rows. Bands come from the workbook's own REVIEW BOARD
  formulas, not a Python reimplementation.
- **Integrity check:** all 8,761 PlayerIds in 008 appear in the scratch build
  with identical Projected band, Elite share, REVIEW?, Speed alert and Traits
  graded (0 mismatches).
- **Matching:** `scripts/validate_recap.py`, normalized name plus a compatible
  position group, then a check on the Telemetry team. 16 matched exactly. Three
  are spelled differently in Telemetry and matched on last name plus first
  initial, confirmed by team and position: Jacob Anderson (Illinois State NT,
  `ILST`, 624 snaps), Yakari Walker (Memphis C) and Kamren Washington (Texas
  State DT). 10 of the 19
  carry Elig 0 and so are absent from 008, which is why the scratch build drops
  the filter.
- Every row has Sample OK (150+ snaps).

## Results

Band gap = projected band minus Baylor RK, in tier steps (AA, AL, QS, FRP, LIM,
NGE).

| Table | Player | Pos | 2025 team | Baylor RK | Traits (elite / graded) | Share | Band | Gap | REVIEW | Speed | Player Impact |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Other | Anthony Colandrea | QB | UNLV | AL | 5 / 10 | .50 | QS | -1 | Y | | 100 |
| Other | Kam Perry | WR (SWR) | Miami (OH) | AL | 3 / 8 | .375 | QS | -1 | Y | | 93 |
| Other | Danny Scudero | WR (SWR) | San Jose St | QS | 3 / 8 | .375 | QS | 0 | Y | Y | 90 |
| Other | Braden Pegan | WR (OWR) | Utah St | QS | 5 / 8 | .625 | AL | +1 | Y | Y | 98 |
| Other | Ben Murawski | OT (LT) | UConn | QS | 1 / 2 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 90 |
| Other | Joe Hjelle | IDL (DT) | Tulsa | AL | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -2 | | | 96 |
| Other | Jordan Sanders | IDL (DT) | Texas St | QS | 2 / 4 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 82 |
| Other | Jake Anderson | IDL (NT) | Illinois St | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 93 |
| Other | Harper Holloman | EDGE (UP) | W. Kentucky | AL | 1 / 6 | .17 | FRP | -2 | | | 93 |
| Baylor | Logan Moore | OT (RT) | UAB | QS | 1 / 2 | .50 | QS | 0 | Y | | 78 |
| Baylor | Asher Hale | OG (RG) | S. Alabama | FRP | 2 / 2 | 1.00 | AA | +3 | Y | | 1 |
| Baylor | Yakiri Walker | C | Memphis | FRP | 0 / 2 | 0 | LIM | -1 | | | 91 |
| Baylor | Cole Rhett | OT (RT) | Toledo | FRP | 0 / 2 | 0 | LIM | -1 | | | 84 |
| Baylor | Jamaal Whyce | IDL (DT) | Marshall | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 92 |
| Baylor | Kam Washington | IDL (DT) | Texas St | QS | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | -1 | | | 82 |
| Baylor | Jordan Mack | IDL (DT) | Coastal Carolina | FRP | 1 / 4 | .25 | FRP | 0 | | | 61 |
| Baylor | Garrick Ponder | EDGE (UP) | Southern Miss | FRP | 2 / 6 | .33 | FRP | 0 | | | 89 |
| Baylor | Kedrick Walker | OB-LB (ILB) | Georgia St | FRP | 3 / 7 | .43 | QS | +1 | Y | Y | 1 |
| Baylor | Stilton McKelvey | CB (OCB) | New Mexico St | FRP | 3 / 5 | .60 | QS | +1 | Y | | 76 |

### Band agreement

- Exact: 6 of 19. Within one tier: 16 of 19.
- Off by two or more: Hjelle (AL to FRP), Holloman (AL to FRP), Hale (FRP to AA).
- The band runs low at the top. Of 4 AL-graded players, none projects AL: 2
  project QS and 2 project FRP. The one AL projection (Pegan) was graded QS.

### REVIEW as a screen

| Baylor RK | REVIEW fired | Not fired |
|---|---|---|
| QS or better (12) | 7 | 5 |
| FRP (7) | 3 | 4 |

- **Offense QS or better: 6 of 6 caught** (Colandrea, Perry, Scudero, Pegan,
  Murawski, Moore).
- **Defensive front QS or better: 1 of 6 caught.** Only Sanders fired. Hjelle,
  Anderson, Whyce and Washington (IDL) and Holloman (EDGE) did not.
- FRP players flagged: Hale, Kedrick Walker, McKelvey.

## Observations (not tuning decisions)

1. **The defensive-front misses share one shape.** Each IDL miss has 1 elite
   trait of 4 (share .25, under the .375 trigger). With only 4 counted traits,
   the IDL gate needs 2 elite. Tackling is the lowest trait for all four and a
   deficiency for three (Anderson 0, Whyce 1, Washington 17; Hjelle 43), and
   Get Off is Whyce's other deficiency (8). Holloman's EDGE line is similar: Get Off 17, CoD 9.
2. **Advanced Stats saw the front-line misses.** All five carry Player Impact 82
   to 96, and Run Stops Over Expected or Disruption sits in the 89th to 99th
   percentile for each IDL (Hjelle RSOE 94, Anderson RSOE 89, Whyce Disruption
   98, Washington Disruption 99). None of those fields feed REVIEW today.
3. **The false positives are the Gravely pattern.** Hale (OG, 2 of 2 elite, AA)
   and Kedrick Walker (ILB, speed alert) both sit at Player Impact 1. Hale also
   has Penalty at the 2nd percentile. Traits look good; production does not. The
   OL two-trait set makes this worse: 2 of 2 is an automatic AA.
4. **OL band is coarse.** With 2 traits, OL shares can only be 0, .5 or 1, so
   OL bands can only be LIM or NGE, QS, or AA. Y. Walker and Rhett land LIM
   (graded FRP) and Hale lands AA (graded FRP).
5. **Offense tracks well.** Every offensive player is within one tier, and the
   QB, WR and OT rows are the closest agreement on the tab.

## Limits of this test

- n = 19, and every one of them earned a Power Four transfer, so the sample has
  no clear negatives (players Baylor graded LIM or NGE). It can show misses on
  good players and flags on FRP players, not how well REVIEW rejects.
- The Baylor grades may have been set after film and portal context the 2025
  data never saw. A gap is a question, not proof the data is wrong.
- Left-table grades are Baylor's read on players who went elsewhere; right-table
  grades are on players Baylor signed. Both are treated the same here.

## Questions for Eric (feed 009)

- Should a high Player Impact (or elite Advanced Stats count) surface a
  defensive-front player whose trait share misses the gate, as a separate alert
  the way the speed alert works? That stays a threshold flag, not a composite.
- Should a very low Player Impact show as a caution on REVIEW rows (Hale,
  Kedrick Walker)?
- Is Tackling the right counted trait for IDL, given it drove three of four
  misses?
- The Power Four validation downloads (Next 2) would add 25 more graded players
  and some LIM-graded rows. Worth doing before 009, so the matrix does not rest
  on 19 players?

## Side notes

- Leaderboard `Team` is the 2025 school (slug for G6, code like `ILST` for FCS),
  not a current value, unlike `Elig.` and `Class`.
- The leaderboard's `Top End Speed` column holds values like 32, 50 and 90 for
  linemen, which look like percentiles, not mph. It feeds no flag. Check before
  quoting it.

# Claude in Chrome browser automation

You have access to browser automation tools (mcp__claude-in-chrome__*) for interacting with web pages in Chrome. Follow these guidelines for effective browser automation.

## Loading deferred tools

If the mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load every tool you expect to need in ONE ToolSearch call — the select query accepts a comma-separated list — never one call per tool. Start with the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting.

## GIF recording

When performing multi-step browser interactions that the user may want to review or share, use mcp__claude-in-chrome__gif_creator to record them.

You must ALWAYS:
* Capture extra frames before and after taking actions to ensure smooth playback
* Name the file meaningfully to help the user identify it later (e.g., "login_process.gif")

## Console log debugging

You can use mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages to read console output. Console output may be verbose. If you are looking for specific log entries, use the 'pattern' parameter with a regex-compatible pattern. This filters results efficiently and avoids overwhelming output. For example, use pattern: "[MyApp]" to filter for application-specific logs rather than reading all console output.

## Alerts and dialogs

IMPORTANT: Do not trigger JavaScript alerts, confirms, prompts, or browser modal dialogs through your actions. These browser dialogs block all further browser events and will prevent the extension from receiving any subsequent commands. Instead, when possible, use console.log for debugging and then use the mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_console_messages tool to read those log messages. If a page has dialog-triggering elements:
1. Avoid clicking buttons or links that may trigger alerts (e.g., "Delete" buttons with confirmation dialogs)
2. If you must interact with such elements, warn the user first that this may interrupt the session
3. Use mcp__claude-in-chrome__javascript_tool to check for and dismiss any existing dialogs before proceeding

If you accidentally trigger a dialog and lose responsiveness, inform the user they need to manually dismiss it in the browser.

## Avoid rabbit holes and loops

When using browser automation tools, stay focused on the specific task. If you encounter any of the following, stop and ask the user for guidance:
- Unexpected complexity or tangential browser exploration
- Browser tool calls failing or returning errors after 2-3 attempts
- No response from the browser extension
- Page elements not responding to clicks or input
- Pages not loading or timing out
- Unable to complete the browser task despite multiple approaches

Explain what you attempted, what went wrong, and ask how the user would like to proceed. Do not keep retrying the same failing browser action or explore unrelated pages without checking in first.

## Tab context and session startup

IMPORTANT: At the start of each browser automation session, call mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp first to get information about the user's current browser tabs. Use this context to understand what the user might want to work with before creating new tabs.

Never reuse tab IDs from a previous/other session. Follow these guidelines:
1. Only reuse an existing tab if the user explicitly asks to work with it
2. Otherwise, create a new tab with mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp
3. If a tool returns an error indicating the tab doesn't exist or is invalid, call tabs_context_mcp to get fresh tab IDs
4. When a tab is closed by the user or a navigation error occurs, call tabs_context_mcp to see what tabs are available

entries.name: mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer
entries.description:
Use a mouse and keyboard to interact with a web browser, and take screenshots. If you don't have a valid tab ID, use tabs_context_mcp first to get available tabs.
* Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element before moving the cursor.
* If you tried clicking on a program or link but it failed to load, even after waiting, try adjusting your click location so that the tip of the cursor visually falls on the element that you want to click.
* Make sure to click any buttons, links, icons, etc with the cursor tip in the center of the element. Don't click boxes on their edges unless asked.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported and will return an error - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels. Requires a Claude in Chrome extension version that supports scale; older extensions return the full-size image.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.
